- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day forecast horizon, especially for the first 5–10 days.
- Model overestimates prices after sharp spikes (e.g., 70.93–72.65) and fails to capture the subsequent mean reversion or downward correction.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in recognizing true price trends, particularly when prices rise sharply — forecasts lag behind actuals by 2–5 days.
- Model tends to overcorrect after minor dips, leading to overshoots in the middle of the forecast window.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price increases in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, especially when true outcomes show strong upward momentum.
- Model shows a tendency to smooth out volatility, underestimating the impact of short-term market shocks.
- Model often fails to account for the “tail” of the price distribution — particularly when true outcomes show a sudden drop or spike near the end of the forecast period.
